text:
Gabe Perreault is 21, in his first real NHL season, and he's scoring like a top-six winger: seven goals and 11 points in 23 games for the Rangers on about 16 and a half minutes a night. One headline already argued the Rangers should lock him up, along with Tye Kartye and Will Cuylle, before their price tags rise.

The scoring looks earned. His 6.7 expected goals is a strong number for his ice time, and he's right on it. The Rangers take 53% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, about even with their rate without him. The Rangers have scored 4.8 more goals than expected with him out there, so the assists may come slower. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) says his offense lives in transition: 60% of his shots come off the rush. His last college season, 60 points at Boston College, translated to about 55 NHL points. Our range projects 34 to 54 points. With injuries piling up in New York, his minutes should keep growing.
